claims.text: In-situ mechanical testing combined with real-time microscopy or diffraction will reveal the microstructural evolution of FeNiCrMn under load and temperature.
Observing microstructural evolution in situ will clarify the mechanisms governing the mechanical performance of FeNiCrMn.
FeNiCrMn is a Co-free high-entropy alloy system.
Mechanical loading from cryogenic to elevated temperatures can be coupled with continuous or quasi-continuous electron microscopy or X-ray diffraction.
Microstructural evolution during deformation may include dislocation motion, twinning, stacking-fault formation, and phase transitions.
These deformation processes can be tracked in real time.
Synergistic interactions among the elements in FeNiCrMn produce distinctive dislocation and twinning behavior.
Localized lattice distortions under stress may cause enhanced strengthening in FeNiCrMn.
Localized lattice distortions under stress may enhance ductility in FeNiCrMn.
FeNiCrMn exhibits temperature-dependent, collaborative dislocation-twinning mechanisms.
Collaborative dislocation-twinning mechanisms enhance the strength and ductility of FeNiCrMn.
FeNiCrMn can deliver competitive mechanical properties while remaining cost-effective.
Prior ex-situ tensile-test data and corrosion evaluations exist for FeNiCrMn.
Established knowledge of CoCrFeMnNi Cantor-type alloys can serve as a baseline for FeNiCrMn.
Very high strain rates may constrain in-situ measurements.
Limited spatial or temporal resolution may prevent real-time detection of small-scale deformation processes.
Achieving the desired spatial and temporal characterization may require specialized equipment or synchrotron beamlines.
